name.zh: 法隆寺地区佛教建筑群
name.en: Buddhist Monuments in the Horyu-ji Area

description.zh: 法隆寺建于7世纪，是世界上现存最古老的木结构建筑群，包含48栋国宝级建筑。五重塔与金堂是飞鸟时代佛教建筑的巅峰之作，于1993年列入UNESCO世界遗产。
description.en: Horyu-ji, built in the 7th century, houses the world's oldest surviving wooden structures. The complex of 48 national-treasure buildings, including the five-storey pagoda and Golden Hall, represents the pinnacle of Asuka-period Buddhist architecture and was UNESCO-listed in 1993.

zh: 世界最古老的木结构建筑群，建于7世纪
五重塔高32.5米，是日本飞鸟时代代表作
珍藏大量国宝级佛教雕塑与文物
en: World's oldest surviving wooden structures, dating to the 7th century
The 32.5 m five-storey pagoda is the masterpiece of Asuka-period architecture
Houses an extraordinary collection of national-treasure Buddhist sculptures

admission.zh: 成人1,500日元（含西院伽蓝与大宝藏院）
admission.en: Adults ¥1,500 (includes West Precinct and Great Treasure Hall)

tips.zh: 从JR法隆寺站步行约20分钟，或乘坐社区巴士。建议配合奈良市区景点一日游。
tips.en: About 20 minutes' walk from JR Horyuji station, or take the community bus. Combine with a day trip to Nara city for maximum efficiency.

description.zh: 奈良曾是日本奈良时代（710—784年）的首都，保存有东大寺（世界最大木构建筑）、春日大社、兴福寺等8处国宝级建筑群，加上奈良公园的野生鹿群，于1998年列入UNESCO世界遗产。
description.en: Nara was Japan's capital during the Nara period (710–784). Eight national-treasure monuments survive, including Todai-ji — home to the world's largest wooden building — Kasuga Taisha and Kofuku-ji, alongside the wild deer of Nara Park. UNESCO-listed in 1998.

zh: 东大寺大佛殿：世界最大木构建筑，内供15米大佛
奈良公园约1,200头自由漫步的野生鹿
春日大社原始森林中的朱红神社建筑群
en: Todai-ji's Great Buddha Hall: the world's largest wooden building, housing a 15 m bronze Buddha
About 1,200 freely roaming wild deer in Nara Park
Kasuga Taisha shrine complex set in ancient primeval forest

admission.zh: 东大寺大仏殿600日元，春日大社宝物殿500日元
admission.en: Todai-ji Great Buddha Hall ¥600; Kasuga Taisha Treasure Hall ¥500

tips.zh: 可从京都乘近铁约45分钟到达，适合日归。鹿饼（鹿せんべい）在各处均有售，可以喂鹿。
tips.en: Easily reached from Kyoto in 45 minutes by Kintetsu rail — perfect for a day trip. Deer crackers (shika senbei) are sold everywhere and the deer are famously polite beggars.
